claims.text: A laser-cladded WVTaTiCr refractory high-entropy-alloy coating with x = 1 can be deposited on a 42-CrMo steel substrate.
The x = 1 composition represents the maximum Cr dosing within the tested WVTaTiCrx series.
42-CrMo and 316L are examples of stainless-steel substrates relevant to the hypothesis.
The coating system can be evaluated by corrosion testing in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
The coating system can be evaluated by high-temperature oxidation at 800 °C for an extended period.
Laser cladding produces a dense and uniform passive oxide film on the coated surface.
The passive film contains Cr2O3, CrTaO4, and TiO2.
Laser cladding creates a refined coating microstructure.
The coating has a single-phase BCC solid-solution microstructure.
High Cr content induces lattice distortion in the coating.
High Cr content promotes precipitation of intermetallic phases such as Cr2Ta.
Cr2Ta intermetallic precipitates act as nucleation sites for a robust passive film.
The passive film limits ion diffusion and oxygen ingress.
Limiting ion diffusion and oxygen ingress reduces corrosion and oxidation rates relative to the bare substrate.
The coated substrate will have a higher corrosion potential than the unmodified substrate.
The coated substrate will have a significantly lower corrosion current density and corrosion rate than the unmodified substrate.
The coating will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the unmodified substrate.
Untreated steel exhibits higher corrosion-current density and deeper corrosion or oxide penetration under comparable conditions.
The magnitude of the beneficial effect depends on the precise coating composition and laser-cladding parameters.
Similar high-entropy-alloy coatings have shown qualitative improvements in corrosion resistance.

contradictions.description: The coating is described as a single-phase BCC solid solution, while the mechanism simultaneously invokes precipitation of a distinct Cr2Ta intermetallic phase; without a temporal or volume-fraction qualification, these descriptions are inconsistent.

The initial material field groups 42-CrMo with stainless steel, whereas the cited system describes 42-CrMo only as a steel substrate and provides no support for treating it as equivalent to a 316L stainless-steel substrate.
